NOTES OV AIRPORT
Friday, Sept. 17, 1926.
At the request of the. Chamber of Commerce and suggested
by the Supervisors attending the luncheon to Assistant Secretary
of the Navy Warner, I met Mr. Warner and the officers of the
Twelfth Naval Division at Harrison and Spear Streets at 2:30 o'clock.
We left about 3:00 o'clock and visited the South San Francisco site
and Millbrae site.
Did not visit the San Mateo site,
as it was not
suitable for hydroplanes.
Returned to San Francisco
at 4:45 o'clock.
The Assistant
Secretary expressed the opinion that the
site at South San Francisco was not admirably adapted for hydro-
planes, as the hydroplane would probably have to taxi at some three
miles before it could start to rise. Depth of water is needed for
hydroplanes, according to the Assistant Secretary, in order to enable
boats to deliver supplies direct to the hydroplanes.
We also visited the Millbrae site and the Assistant
Secretary said that it appeared to him that this was a much better
Not being familiar with the direction of the winds at all
times he could not state whether it was ideal or not.
He also asked
concerning drainage on both sites and whether during
the winter
the land would be waterlogged.
He also made the statement
that if it were a question of securing a field not suitable for
hydroplanes but absolutely clear of fog, that he would select that
field rather than take a field suitable
fog at times.

Mr. Guersey of the Chamber of Commerce accompanied the
party; also Rear-Admiral Thomas Washington Lieutenant Commander B
Rear-Admiral Peeples, of the Supply Corps,
Commandant of the District,
G. Leighton, Aide of
the Assistant Secretary and Commander C. J.
Foy.

NOTES
ON AIRPORT
Tuesday, Sept. 14, 1926.
Called on Mr. Shaw, South San Francisco Land and Improve-
ment Company, Merchants Exchange Building.
Suggested that the limit to be paid by the City for the
100 acres involved in site No. 2 would be $260,000.00, provided that
the land be brought to an elevation of plus 10
feet by the present
owner; that in addition, the land Company would have to include
a right of way for a spur track from the Belt Railroad into the
proposed aeroplane site.
Mr. Shaw stated that if we submitted the offer it would
be forwarded to his company, but that he would not recommend its
acceptance.
Mr. Shaw's price on the above site as per the conditions
mentioned
above is $340,000.00 for an area of approximately 100
acres.
*******
Tuesday,
Sent. 14
14:00 P. M.)
1926.
Called on Mr. Medina, Mr. Howard Sr. and Mr. Howard Jr.,
Bank of California, in re site
No. 1.
They agreed to sell to the City all land that we wish
east of the present transmission line and including the land on
both sides of the Bay Shore Boulevard, with the exception of two
easements for road purposes at the northerly and southerly
boundaries, these easements to be used for road purposes only.
Would deliver the same subject to confirmation on the part of
Taylor for $2,000.00 per acre.
I stated to them that the price should be between $750.00
and $1,000.00 per acre, and requested them to submit this proposi-
tion to their principals.
Mr. Howard Sr. said that he would leave
Wednesday morning and would give me an answer by the 20th or the
21st of September.
